body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the current application, of which claims 15-20 are withdrawn.
Claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 because the claimed invention is allegedly directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.

Claims 1-14 are rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of Alspach, U.S. Patent No. 11,536,621, which was published as U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0302249.
Claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by Alspach.

Claims 1 and 8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sakuma (T. Sakuma, E. Phillips, G. A.G. Ricardez, M. Ding, J. Takamatsu and T. Ogasawara, "A Parallel Gripper with a Universal Fingertip Device Using Optical Sensing and Jamming Transition for Maintaining Stable Grasps") in further view of Rogers (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2012/0261551 to Rogers).
Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the remarks and amendments submitted herewith.

Claims 1, 4, 8, and 11 have been amended as shown herein. Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures and claims as originally filed, and more specifically, in at least paragraphs [0040]-[0041 and [0066] and FIGs. 5, 7, and 10A-10C. No new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.

Attorney Wuennenberg thank Examiner Rahmjoo for the telephonic interview of June 11, 2024. The specification, claims and drawings of the instant application were discussed in view of the cited references. Additionally, proposed amendments to the claims were presented and
discussed in view of the asserted rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102(a)(2), and 103, and the double patenting rejection. Agreement was not reached regarding the claims.
Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as this statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.133.
As mentioned hereinabove, claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to ineligible subject matter. The rejections are respectfully traversed.

The Examiner asserts that recited method of calibrating a deformable sensor is allegedly directed to an abstract idea that is not integrated into a practical application because the steps allegedly recite words of "apply it" without additional steps that cannot be done mentally. (Office Action, pg. 5). Applicant has amended the independent claims are presented herein and respectfully submits that the claims, as amended, are patent eligible under 35 U.S.C. § 101.

Independent claim 1 is amended to recite, in part, "capturing image data of the deformable sensor using an external image sensor, wherein the deformable sensor comprises a deformable membrane defining an enclosure that is configured to be filled with a medium, and the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane; comparing the image data of the deformable sensor to a metric to generate a similarity value defining a degree of a difference between the deformable membrane in the image data and a geometry of the deformable membrane corresponding to the metric; and adjusting a pressure within the enclosure based on the similarity value." Independent claim 8 is similarly amended.

Applicant respectfully submits that at least the aforementioned recitation of the claims provides additional elements beyond the alleged abstract idea. Moreover, the recited features, for example, "the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane" and "comparing the image data of the deformable sensor to a metric to generate a similarity value defining a degree of a difference between the deformable membrane in the image data and a

geometry of the deformable membrane corresponding to the metric" recite particular structural features of the deformable sensor thus integrating the subject matter into a practical application and further include additional elements that are sufficient to amount to significantly more than the judicial exception because the steps of the claims cannot be done mentally.

Applicant respectfully submits the recited technical features of amended independent claims 1 and 8 provide improvements to the technical field of deformable sensors and provide technical benefits or more accurate detections of the type of an object and/or a pose of an object as a result of the calibration processes and systems recited in the claims. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claims 1 and 8 and all claims that depend therefrom are patent eligible under 35 U.S.C. § 101. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 101 is respectfully requested.

As noted hereinabove, claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by Alspach. Claims 1 and 8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sakuma and in further view of Rogers. The rejections are respectfully traversed.

For a prior art reference to anticipate a claim, "the identical invention must be shown [in the prior art reference] in as complete detail as is contained in the claim." MPEP § 2131 (quoting Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236 (Fed. Cir. 1989)). A claim may be anticipated by a prior art reference "only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." Id. (quoting Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631 (Fed. Cir. 1987)).

Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claims are not anticipated by or obvious in view of the cited references. Independent claim 1 is amended to recite, in part, "capturing image data of the deformable sensor using an external image sensor, wherein the deformable sensor comprises a deformable membrane defining an enclosure that is configured to be filled with a medium, and the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane; comparing the image data of the deformable sensor to a metric to generate a similarity

value defining a degree of a difference between the deformable membrane in the image data and a geometry of the deformable membrane corresponding to the metric; and adjusting a pressure within the enclosure based on the similarity value." Independent claim 8 is similarly amended.

Alspach discusses a deformable membrane and an internal sensor. Additionally, aspects appear to be directed to time-of-flight sensors for detecting deformation of the membrane. Alspach does not appear to disclose, teach, or suggest "capturing image data of the deformable sensor using an external image sensor, wherein the deformable sensor comprises a deformable membrane defining an enclosure that is configured to be filled with a medium, and the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane; comparing the image data of the deformable sensor to a metric to generate a similarity value defining a degree of a difference between the deformable membrane in the image data and a geometry of the deformable membrane corresponding to the metric; and adjusting a pressure within the enclosure based on the similarity value," as recited in amended independent claim 1 and as similarly recited in amended independent claim 8.

Sakuma appears to discuss a parallel gripper with a universal fingertip device that combines both object holding using jamming transition and optical sensing. However, there does not appear to be any discussion of a method of calibrating a deformable sensor comprising "capturing image data of the deformable sensor using an external image sensor, wherein the deformable sensor comprises a deformable membrane defining an enclosure that is configured to be filled with a medium, and the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane; comparing the image data of the deformable sensor to a metric to generate a similarity value defining a degree of a difference between the deformable membrane in the image data and a geometry of the deformable membrane corresponding to the metric; and adjusting a pressure within the enclosure based on the similarity value," as recited in amended independent claim 1 and as similarly recited in amended independent claim 8.

Furthermore, portions of Rogers discuss patterning detector arrays with an array of sensors, but Rogers does not discuss patterning a membrane or applying a filter a deformable membrane which is viewed by an internal sensor to capture images thereof and determine deformations from

the captured images. More specifically, Rogers does not teach or suggest, at least the recited features: "wherein the deformable sensor comprises a deformable membrane defining an enclosure that is configured to be filled with a medium, and the deformable membrane comprises a filter layer on a surface of the deformable membrane configured to assist in detection of a deformation of the deformable membrane" as recited in amended independent claim 1 and as similarly recited in amended independent claim 8.

Accordingly, for at least the foregoing reasons and the amendments to the claims, Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claims 1 and 8 and all claims that depend therefrom are patentable over Alspach, Sakuma, and Rogers, alone or in combination. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102(a)(2) and 103 is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-14 are rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,536,621.

Applicant respectfully submits that the nonstatutory double patenting rejection is traversed in view of the amendments to independent claims 1 and 8. Independent claims 1 and 8 are amended to recite patentably distinct features from U.S. Patent No. 11,536,621. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the non-statutory double patenting rejection in view of the amendments to the claims presented herein.

In view of the above remarks and amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response. Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.
